title: Billing counts that grow after a crash
description: Your click aggregator consumes Kafka, dedupes by click ID in an in-memory set, and every minute runs UPDATE agg SET clicks = clicks + n for each ad. After a processor node crashed and restarted from the last committed offsets, several advertisers' counts for the previous 10 minutes are about 15% higher than the raw event archive shows. What is the right fix?

options.text: Commit Kafka offsets after every single event instead of every few seconds
options.explanation: Smaller gaps reduce but do not remove the replay window, and per-event commits hurt throughput; the in-memory dedupe set and additive sink remain wrong on replay.

options.text: Checkpoint dedupe state together with consumer offsets, and write window results as upserts that set the count for (adId, bucket) rather than incrementing it
options.explanation: Restoring state and offsets together means replayed events are recognised, and a set-based upsert makes re-emitting a window idempotent, so a crash cannot inflate counts.

options.text: Move dedupe to the query service by running COUNT DISTINCT over raw click IDs on every dashboard request
options.explanation: Correct in principle but it scans raw events on the latency-sensitive path, which cannot meet a 1-second p99 over 90 days.

options.text: Switch the click redirect from 302 to 301 so fewer duplicate clicks reach the service
options.explanation: Browser-cached 301s would bypass the click service entirely and lose clicks, and the inflation here comes from replays, not user double-clicks.
